vocabulary.meaning_en: a hard hit; a sudden disappointment

vocabulary.meaning_en: not as good as you hoped

vocabulary.example: Grandad told us a tale about his village.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (formal, old) by that; because of that
vocabulary.note_ar: تُستخدم غالباً في تعابير ثابتة مثل thereby hangs a tale.
vocabulary.note_en: Mostly used in fixed phrases like 'thereby hangs a tale'.
vocabulary.example: He trained every day, thereby improving his time.

fine_lines.title: A doddle vs a flying start
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a doddle تعني أن مهمة ما سهلة جداً. a flying start تعني بداية ممتازة وسريعة لشيء ما.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'A doddle' = a very easy task. 'A flying start' = a very good, fast beginning.

examples.sentence: Our team got off to a flying start with two early goals.

fine_lines.title: A blow vs a thing
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a blow حدث مخيّب أو صدمة سيئة. a thing (بمعنى is it a thing?) شيء صار رائجاً وشائعاً. معنيان مختلفان تماماً رغم أن كلاهما يبدأ بـ a.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'A blow' is a disappointment or shock. 'A thing' (as in 'Is that a thing now?') is something that has become popular or common. Very different meanings.

examples.sentence: Losing my job was a big blow.
Cold coffee drinks are a thing now.

fine_lines.title: Have a pop vs play a blinder
fine_lines.explanation_ar: have a pop (at something) تعني أن تجرّب أو تحاول شيئاً، دون ضمان النجاح. play a blinder تعني أن تؤدي أداءً ممتازاً جداً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Have a pop at something' = try it, without knowing if you'll succeed. 'Play a blinder' = perform extremely well.

examples.sentence: I've never made bread, but I'll have a pop at it.

expressions.meaning_en: (UK, informal) something very easy to do
expressions.example: Setting up the new phone was a doddle.

expressions.meaning_en: (informal) something that has become popular or fashionable
expressions.example: Is eating breakfast for dinner a thing now?
It was a blow when the trip was cancelled.

expressions.meaning_en: there's an interesting story behind that (from Shakespeare)
expressions.example: 'Why is your car painted pink?' - 'Thereby hangs a tale.'
I'll have a pop at fixing the tap myself.
Our team played a blinder in the final.

expressions.phrase: light up like a Christmas tree
expressions.meaning_en: to suddenly look very happy and excited
expressions.example: When my son saw the new bike, he lit up like a Christmas tree.
She got off to a flying start in her new school.

grammar.title: Using 'a' in fixed expressions
grammar.explanation_ar: في هذه التعابير يأتي a قبل الاسم ولا يُحذف: It's a doddle، It was a blow، get off to a flying start، have a pop. ولاحظ: is it a thing? تعني هل صار رائجاً؟
grammar.explanation_en: In these expressions 'a' comes before the noun and can't be dropped: It's a doddle, It was a blow, get off to a flying start, have a pop. Note: 'Is it a thing?' asks if it's popular now.
examples: We got off to a flying start.
I'll have a pop at it.
